title: Prescriptions Class Schedule of Days Supply, Split Fills and Generic Substitution
content:
For Kestrel Prescriptions, the handling class of a prescription sets how large or small one fill may be, whether a 90-day supply is available, whether therapy starts with split fills, and whether an A-rated generic is the default product.

## Days supply per fill

| Handling class | Smallest days supply per fill | Largest days supply per fill | 90-day supply allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Controlled Acute Prescription | 1 | 30 | No |
| Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription | 7 | 90 | Yes |
| Schedule V Controlled Prescription | 7 | 90 | Yes |
| Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription | 3 | 30 | No |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 1 | 30 | No |
| Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription | 7 | 30 | No |

The smallest and largest days supply are whole days and bound one fill of the class. Where the class allows a 90-day supply, a fill may be dispensed as a 90-day supply; where it does not, it may not.

## Split fills at the start of therapy and generic default

| Handling class | Days supply of each split fill | Number of initial fills dispensed as split fills | A-rated generic dispensed by default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Controlled Acute Prescription | 0 (no split fill) | 0 | Yes |
| Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription | 0 (no split fill) | 0 | Yes |
| Schedule V Controlled Prescription | 0 (no split fill) | 0 | Yes |
| Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription | 0 (no split fill) | 0 | Yes |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 0 (no split fill) | 0 | Yes |
| Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription | 15 | 2 | No |

A split-fill days supply of 0 means the class has no split fill. Where the generic default is Yes, an A-rated generic is dispensed unless the prescriber wrote dispense-as-written; where it is No, the class carries no such default.

## Points of reading (hypothetical figures)

- A Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription fill of 2 days supply is below that class's smallest fill of 3 days; a fill of 30 days is the largest the class allows.
- A Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription starts therapy with 2 split fills of 15 days supply each.
- A Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription may be dispensed as a 90-day supply; a Non-Controlled Acute Prescription may not, its largest fill being 30 days.
